content: Adam Neely: bass guitar, synthesizers, production, string and horn arrangements, some vocals. Shawn Crowder: drums, percussion, electronic percussion; Touch Guitar on one track.
parameters: 2 core players. Each release adds guests: 3 guests (2014), 4 (2019), 11 names (2021), 18 names (2024)

content: Four players on stage: bass, drums, and two of tenor sax, guitar, keys. 2022: keys with sax or guitar. 2025: tenor sax (Jared Yee) and guitar (Joshua De La Victoria), no keyboard player.
parameters: 4 players. Neely calls it an instrumental four-piece jazz fusion band

item: Forces of the 2024 album, by track
content: Tenor sax on 8 of 9 tracks. Guitar on 6 of 9 tracks, by four guitarists. A keyboard guest on 6 of 9. String quartet on 3. Horn section on 2.
parameters: Tenor sax (Jared Yee): 1 to 8. Guitar: De La Victoria (1, 7), Plini (2), Lettieri (3), Saran (4, 6). Keys: Salami (2, 5, 7, 9), Button Masher (4), Li (8). Strings: 2, 6, 9. Horns: 3, 6
where: Against the Fall of Night (2024), credit track numbers

content: A horn section of five players, arranged by Neely. With the tenor sax soloist there are six winds.
parameters: Flute (Josh Plotner), trumpet (Allison Phillips), alto sax (Brian Plautz), baritone sax (Steven Chen), trombone (Jacob Melsha). Credit tracks 3 and 6

content: A string quartet arranged by Neely. The 2021 album has a string group on one track.
parameters: 2 violins (Caleb Burhans, Tomoko Akaboshi), viola (Kayla Williams), cello (Hamilton Berry). Credit tracks 2, 6, 9. 2021: The Resonance Collective on track 4
where: Against the Fall of Night (2024); Perihelion (2021)

content: One track adds Irish and folk colours: tin whistle, Irish flute, uilleann pipes, banjo, acoustic guitar. Another track adds a percussion player. Neely names Irish traditional music and desert blues as sources of Whisky and Mes.
parameters: Credit track 6: Josh Plotner (tin whistle, Irish flute, uilleann pipes), Shubh Saran (banjo, acoustic guitar). Credit track 3: Josh Bailey (percussion). Caution: the Bandcamp page lists Whisky and Mes as track 5 and Oeteldonk as 6; another listing has the opposite order, so it is not certain which piece is credit track 6

content: 2021: voices on 4 of 10 tracks; wind guests are shakuhachi, alto sax, tenor sax, bass clarinet. On the EPs each track adds one guest colour to the duo.
parameters: 2021: voices Hannah Sumner (4, 9), Jae Soto (6), Neely (10); shakuhachi (1) and alto sax (5) Zac Zinger; tenor sax Jared Yee (3, 5, 7, 9, 10); bass clarinet Brian Krock (10); piano and synths Christian Li (2, 4, 9); guitar Tom Monda (3), Shubh Saran (5, 6), De La Victoria (7). 2019: EWI, guitar, violin, sax. 2014: trumpet, piano and synths, voice; also baritone ukulele (Neely) and iPad synthesizers (Crowder)

content: Three keyboard players take turns: Pier Luigi Salami, Christian Li, and Button Masher (Jake Silverman). Button Masher uses sounds in the style of the Super Nintendo and the Sega Genesis inside the fusion music.
parameters: Christian Li was the usual tour keyboard player in 2022. Pier Luigi Salami joined for the 2022 Europe tour. Button Masher: guest on a Europe tour and on one 2024 track

content: Guitar players take turns: Joshua De La Victoria (from progressive rock and progressive metal), Shubh Saran, earlier Elliott Klein and Tom Monda. Guests: Plini (Australian progressive and fusion guitarist) and Mark Lettieri (Snarky Puppy; known for baritone guitar). No source read gives the number of strings of the guitars in the band; De La Victoria's lesson page says only that he often teaches players of 7-string and 8-string guitars.
parameters: De La Victoria's own releases: Iris, Kepler and five more; his site also lists releases with Intervals and Portraits
source: ha-interview; bc-atfon; bc-perihelion; wiki-lettieri; wiki-plini; delavictoria-site; delavictoria-lessons

content: Pearl kits. The maple MCX kit is on every Sungazer recording. The hi-hat is closed with a remote pedal under the right foot. The video kit has a second snare on the left, tuned low.
parameters: MCX: 20-inch kick, 10, 12, 14-inch toms, 14-inch snare. Reference One: 22-inch kick, 10, 12, 16-inch toms, 14x5-inch snare. Remote hi-hat pedal: Pearl RH-2000. No kick pedal is listed, so a double pedal is not confirmed

content: Dry and 'trashy' cymbals and several stacks.
parameters: Meinl: 16-inch Byzance Extra Dry Medium Thin hi-hats; 22-inch Extra Dry Thin ride; 18-inch Jazz Extra Thin crash; 20-inch Extra Dry Thin crash; 16-inch Classics Custom Trash Stack; stack of two 18-inch trash crashes; two 12-inch trash splashes; 8-inch bell; Ching Ring; Ajuch bells. A transcriber counts at least three stacks
where: Crowder's gear page; Meinl artist page; drum transcription

content: Five-string bass. Neely prefers a low B string for the weight in the subwoofer. In 2024 he also strung a five-string with a high C to play melodies, fourths and chords (the captions name the bass 'Kel', probably his Kiesel). A community list gives a Kiesel JB5 with fanned frets, a Fender Precision with DiMarzio Split P pickups as main bass, and a Dingwall Afterburner II in 2019. He often takes a Moog Sub Phatty on stage as keyboard bass with filter sweeps; one 2021 track made him work a synth bass patch live, and later he decided to stay with the bass guitar.
parameters: 5 strings. Tuning B-E-A-D-G (low B) or E-A-D-G-C (high C). 1 analogue mono synth. 2013 list: Ibanez BTB1005E five-string, Fender Precision, Washburn AB-40 acoustic bass
where: Question-and-answer videos 2023 and 2024; gear lists; interview 2025

content: 21 players.
parameters: Bass with key bass; 4 keyboard players (one also trumpet); 3 guitars (2 also baritone guitar); 1 drummer; 3 percussionists; 2 trumpets/flugelhorns; 1 tenor sax; 1 trombone; 3 violins; 1 viola; 1 cello

content: 20 players; 18 on most tracks.
parameters: Electric bass with Moog key bass; 4 keyboard players (acoustic piano, 2 Fender Rhodes, Hammond B3, Moog, other keyboards); 3 electric guitars; 2 trumpets/flugelhorns; 2 tenor saxes (one also bass clarinet and flute); 1 drummer; 1 percussionist (2 more on tracks 4 and 7); string quartet (2 violins, viola, cello)

content: Band: 12 players. Orchestra: 51 players and a conductor. League took out the oboes, the bassoons, and other instruments of the middle and high range. He added low brass, strings, bass clarinet, and contrabass clarinet for a grittier, heavier sound.
parameters: Band: bass with Moog key bass; 3 guitars; 3 keyboard players (piano, Wurlitzer, organ, clavinet, Fender Rhodes; each has a Moog); 2 trumpets/flugelhorns; 1 tenor sax with clarinet and bass clarinet; drums; percussion. Orchestra: strings 10-8-6-5-3; 3 flutes; 5 clarinets and saxophones (with bass and contrabass clarinet); 4 horns; 3 trombones; bass trombone; tuba; 2 percussion. No trumpets and no harp in the list

content: 20 players in total. 9 to 17 players on one track (median 14).
parameters: 1 bass player; 5 keyboard players (one plays only vocoder and talkbox); 3 guitars; 2 trumpets/flugelhorns; 2 reeds; 1 violin; 3 percussionists; 3 drummers, 2 on each track

content: 17 players.
parameters: Organ; Fender Rhodes; piano; clavinet with Minimoog; electric bass with Moog Sub Phatty; 1 electric guitar; 1 baritone guitar; 2 trumpets; 2 tenor saxes (one also flute); violin; 2 drummers; 3 percussionists (trap set and floor tom; timbal, repinique, kanjira; djembe, shakers)

content: Chonks: 19 players. Xavi: 19 players. Bad Kids to the Back: 18 players. All 3 drummers play on each of the 8 tracks. 3 percussionists play on 7 of the 8 tracks.
parameters: Chonks: 3 electric guitars; electric bass with Minimoog bass; Fender Rhodes; Mellotron; clavinet; Minimoog; 2 trumpets/flugelhorns; 2 tenor saxes (one also flutes and bass clarinet); violin; 3 percussionists; 3 drummers. Xavi: a baritone guitar in place of 1 guitar; percussion on Moroccan darbuka, bendir, and krakeb. Bad Kids: Prophet, Fender Rhodes, Hammond B3, clavinet; Minimoog bass by a keyboard player

content: 19 players at one time: 3 guitars, 4 keyboard players, 2 brass, 2 reeds, 1 violin, 3 percussionists, 3 drummers, 1 bass. A guest keyboard player on 1 track.
parameters: Keyboards: Wurlitzer 200A, Prophet-10, 3 Minimoog Model D, Fender Rhodes Mark 8, Yamaha CP70, Hammond B3, Hohner D6 clavinet, ARP String Ensemble, Mellotron, Korg Kronos, Moog Little Phatty, talkbox, vocoder

content: 73 players: 20 in the band and 53 in the orchestra.
parameters: Band: bass with Minimoog; 3 keyboard players; 3 guitars; 4 drummers; 4 percussionists; 1 violin; 4 horns. Orchestra: strings 9-8-6-4-3; 3 flutes; 2 oboes/English horn; saxophones and clarinets; 3 trumpets; 3 trombones; bass trombone; tuba; 2 percussion; harp

item: Size of the band on stage
content: The band started in 2004 with 10 players. About 20 members are in rotation. 10 to 19 play at one time. The band toured with as many as 13.
parameters: Concert of 14 November 2019: 13 players: 1 guitar; 1 violin; 4 keyboards (one also trumpet, one also talkbox); 1 trumpet/flugelhorn; 2 tenor saxes (one also flutes); 1 drummer; 2 percussionists; bass with Moog key bass. 1 guest on krakeb for 1 track. A concert of 2015: 9 players (drums, percussion, keyboards/trumpet, trumpet, 2 tenor saxes, 2 guitars, bass)
where: Live at the Royal Albert Hall; a concert in Seattle (2015)

content: 2 trumpets (also flugelhorns) and 1 or 2 tenor saxes. A keyboard player adds a 3rd trumpet. The section has more trumpets than reeds.
parameters: Reed doubles: flute, alto flute, bass clarinet, clarinet, soprano sax. A trombone plays on groundUP only. 4 horns (3 trumpets, 1 sax) play Quarter Master as a section feature

item: Strings, drummers, and percussionists for each album

parameters: 5 saxes (2 alto, 2 tenor, 1 baritone); 4 trumpets; 3 trombones and 1 bass trombone; guitar; synth; bass; drums. 4 tracks of 2:33 to 4:55

content: A funk band from Dallas that is led by drums and percussion. It started in 2014 as a duo of a Snarky Puppy drummer and a Snarky Puppy percussionist. The drummer: "too jazzy to be a real funk band, too funky to be a real jazz band" (translated).
parameters: About 9 members in rotation: drums; percussion; 1-2 basses; 2 keyboards; 3 saxes/flutes; trombone; 2 guitars. The first album (2015) was made mostly from overdubs

item: Horn section with rhythm section; 3 registers of strings
content: Cory Wong's show band: 6 horns with a rhythm section of 5. The Fearless Flyers (Wong, Mark Lettieri, Joe Dart, Nate Smith): guitar, baritone guitar, and bass cover 3 registers; the drum kit is only snare, kick, and hi-hat.
parameters: Wong: 3 saxes (flute and clarinet doubles), 2 trumpets, 1 trombone; guitar, bass, keys, percussion, drums; a clean guitar tone with the rhythm guitar at the front. Flyers: 4 players; 3 saxophones as guests on one album (2020)
where: Cory and the Wongnotes (2021); The Fearless Flyers (from 2018)

content: A jazz and pop orchestra: big band and symphony orchestra together. 52 to 97 musicians.
parameters: A double rhythm section: one for pop and rock, one for jazz. Conductor Jules Buckley (2013-2020 and from 2023). Also on a live album with Cory Wong (2020)

content: Two members make the studio tracks. A five-piece band plays live from 2016.
parameters: Cole: drums, keyboards, guitar, bass, voice. Artadi: voice, keyboards, bass. Live: drums, voice, 1 or 2 keyboards, electric bass, saxophone

content: The band tracks use drums, electric bass and keyboards.
parameters: 9 band tracks: 2 keyboards on 8 tracks, 1 keyboard on 1 track; saxophone on 4; guitar on 2. Bass: Sam Wilkes on 5 tracks, MonoNeon on 4. Example "Do Hot Girls Like Chords?": voice, drums, bass, 2 keyboards, guitar; 3:32; 111 BPM (database)

content: Strings, brass, flutes and a choir are added to the band.
parameters: Strings 8-4-4-2 (violins, violas, cellos, basses). Brass: 4 trumpets, 3 trombones, 1 bass trombone, 2 sousaphones, 1 tuba. 3 flutes. Choir of 17

content: A small kit for recording at home.
parameters: Ludwig Black Magic snare; 1969 Gretsch 18-inch bass drum (he uses 18 or 16 inch); Pearl toms; Vic Firth sticks

content: Keys and drums only. The keyboard player gives the bass.
parameters: The Prophet-10 synth is used mostly for bass parts. Bass pedals at the Tiny Desk. Both members also sing

content: Small MIDI keyboards and stage keyboards.
parameters: A 49-key MIDI keyboard on the album. Two stacked Nord keyboards at the Tiny Desk. Sequential Prophet-10 and Prophet X. Gear page (weak evidence): Nord Stage 3, Nord Wave 2, M-Audio Keystation 49es

content: A basic kit, often with no toms. Splash cymbals lie on the snare drums.
parameters: Zildjian session: 3 snares with splashes of 8, 6 and 10 inches on the heads; a stack of 10-inch and 6-inch splashes; 16-inch crashes as hi-hats; one 17-inch crash

content: Four members: three players and a sound engineer who plays the mixing desk. The bass player copies sequenced synth bass lines on bass guitar and pedalboard in real time.
parameters: Drums; bass guitar with pedalboard; keys and synths; sound and "real time audio deconstruction". Earlier line-up: drums, bass, synthesizers, audio deconstruction

content: A small kit with two snares and a wide range of pitch.
parameters: Bass drum 20 x 16 on tour (he says that he prefers 14-inch bass drums). Snares 14 x 5.5 and 14 x 5 (2018), or 13 and 14 inch (2019). Tom 10 x 8; floor tom 14 x 14. Hi-hats of 14 and 10 inches; stack of 14-inch China + 13-inch hi-hat top with holes; 19-inch crash; crash-ride

content: Drums, electric bass, keyboards and electronics.
parameters: Album: drums and synthesizer (leader); 4 electric bass players; 3 keyboard players; 1 percussionist; 2 players of electronics; 4 voices. Live: 2 keyboards, electric bass, drums
where: Beat Music! Beat Music! Beat Music!

content: Dark cymbals. Stacks give short sounds.
parameters: Sabian from about 2006: thin rides; "short trashy sounds" from stacks; a 23-inch prototype as his main cymbal. Zildjian from September 2020: 14-inch hi-hats; 20-inch and 21-inch crash-rides; 20-inch flat ride

content: Drums with pads; keys with pad controllers; a laptop with a click track.
parameters: Drummer: acoustic kit and percussion with 24 pads. Keys player: keyboard, 4 x 4 pad grid, monome grid controller. Ableton Live

content: Eight-string guitars one half step below standard eight-string tuning. The lowest string is F. The seven-string period used B standard one half step down.
parameters: Eight-string: F Bb Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb (low to high); lowest F1 = 43.65 Hz. Album Nothing: E A D G C F A D; lowest E1 = 41.20 Hz. Seven-string (to 1998): Bb Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb; lowest Bb1 = 58.27 Hz. Frequencies computed for A4 = 440 Hz

content: Signature eight-string with a very long scale, one bridge pickup and a fixed bridge. The pickup is 'flat': it adds no power of its own.
parameters: Ibanez M8M: scale 29.4 inches, one Lundgren M8 humbucker, alder body, maple and bubinga neck through the body. Other scales in the band: 27 and 28 inches. Strings for 29.4 inches: .009 .011 .016 .026 .036 .046 .052 .070. Later set .010 to .075. Pick 1 mm nylon

content: Five-string bass played with a pick through an overdrive. It plays the guitar riff, typically one octave below the rhythm guitars.
parameters: Tuning Bb F Bb Eb Ab (low to high); lowest Bb0 = 29.14 Hz (computed). A four-string bass tuned down 1.5 steps for 'Bleed'. Inference from the tunings: the F string of the bass (F1) has the same pitch as the lowest guitar string, so the octave below exists only from Bb up

content: The seventh string adds a low B. The eighth string adds a low F sharp. Many players tune the eighth string down to E, the pitch of the lowest string of a bass guitar.
parameters: 7-string: B1 E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4 (B1 = 61.74 Hz). 8-string: F#1 B1 E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4 (F#1 = 46.25 Hz). First mass-produced 8-string (Ibanez RG2228, 2007): scale 27 inches, factory tuning F1 A#1 D#2 G#2 C#3 F#3 A#3 D#4, gauges .065 .054 .042 .032 .024 .016 .011 .009. Frequencies computed

content: Eight-string in 'drop E'. The three lowest strings give root, fifth and octave under one finger, as in drop D on a six-string. The upper six strings stay in standard tuning.
parameters: E B E A D G B E (low to high); lowest E1 = 41.20 Hz (computed). One song ('Physical Education') uses guitars whose two lowest strings reach down to C#. Strings .009 to .074 (Abasi) and .010 to .074 (Reyes); picks .55 mm and .80 mm

content: Two eight-string guitars and drums. There is no bass player: the low strings of the guitars take the bass register. On the records, a producer or a guitarist adds bass guitar and synthesizers.
parameters: Trio since 2012. Guitars: Ibanez TAM100 (2013, DiMarzio Ionizer pickups), then Abasi Concepts Larada (eight strings, multi-scale with fanned frets, Fishman Fluence pickups with a single-coil voice). Music Man Kaizen 7-string: multi-scale 24.75 to 25.5 inches, low B string 25.65 inches
source: wiki-aal; wiki-abasi; mr-larada; gw-8-string; gw-abasi-lesson; mm-kaizen

content: Headless six-string signature guitar in a drop tuning. The band is guitar, bass guitar and drums. Guests add piano and synthesizer, saxophone, harp, violin and cello, and wordless voices.
parameters: Typical tuning Drop C#: C# G# C# F# A# D# (low to high); lowest C#2 = 69.30 Hz (computed). Two humbuckers (Suhr SSH+ and SSV, later a signature set), 3-way switch with a split-coil middle position, no tone control. The signature guitar plays about 95% of Impulse Voices; a borrowed 7-string plays the lower parts

item: Line-ups of the bright fusion bands
content: Arch Echo is a quintet with keyboards and two guitars as lead voices. Owane is one player who writes, programs and records guitar, synthesizer and bass; a drummer and guests complete some releases.
parameters: Arch Echo: keyboards (Joey Izzo), guitars (Adam Rafowitz, Adam Bentley), bass (Joe Calderone), drums (Richie Martinez); formed 2016, Nashville; Bentley plays 7-string Jackson models. Owane: drums by Maciej Dzik; guests on saxophone, violin and bass guitar

parameters: Mockroot: Sam Minaie (bass guitar), Arthur Hnatek (drums, live electronics). The Call Within: Evan Marien (electric bass), Arthur Hnatek (drums); Hamasyan also plays electronic drums and effects

content: Two bass drums (not a double pedal on one drum) for both drummers. Garstka does not tune the drums high: he wants low punch. He says that his mind is jazz and his heart is rock.
parameters: Haake: two 22x18-inch bass drums, 14x6-inch bronze snare. Garstka: two 22x16-inch bass drums; toms 10x8, 12x8, 14x14, 16x16 inches; purpleheart snare

content: The darker branch of the style uses six-string baritone guitars with a very low sixth string and high string action.
parameters: Scale 27 or 28 inches; one model has 27 frets; Lundgren M6 or M7 pickups. Tunings: E1 C2 F2 A#2 D#3 G#3 (the source prints D#2 for the fifth note) and E1 B1 E2 A2 Ab3 A3. Lowest E1 = 41.20 Hz (computed)

content: The keyboard lead is a layer of a workstation keyboard sound and a software synthesizer. The player bends into target notes as a guitarist does.
parameters: Yamaha Motif sound plus the Massive software synth in MainStage. Pitch-bend range 2 semitones up and 12 semitones down. Aftertouch fades in an upper octave. Two-hand runs with repeated left-hand notes, shown in A Lydian. From a summary page of his video, probably automatic; not confirmed in a primary source

content: The size of the band changes from one record to the next.
parameters: 11 players (Heliocentric Worlds Vol. 1, 1965). 15 on the album The Magic City (1965). 13 (Atlantis). 12 players and 4 singers (Space Is the Place, 1972). 17 (Lanquidity, 1978). 22 people with 3 dancers and a fire-eater (festivals of 1970). 20 to 30 on the tour of 1968
source: wiki-helio1; wiki-magiccity; wiki-atlantis; wiki-spaceplace; wiki-lanquidity; wiki-afterend; wiki-sunra

content: Most saxophone players also play flute, oboe, or clarinet. All members also play percussion.

content: The highest and the lowest registers of the band get the emphasis. They play against each other.
parameters: High: trumpet, piccolo. Low: trombone, bass trombone, baritone sax, bass clarinet, timpani, bass, bass marimba
where: The Heliocentric Worlds of Sun Ra Vol. 1

content: Three horns and three rhythm players. A synthesizer player makes seven.

content: One keyboard player, one reed player, bass, drums, and percussion. No guitar and no brass.

Bass guitar. Drums. Percussion: 9 instruments (agogô, balafon, cabasa, congas, gankogui, log drum, shekere, surdo, tambourine)

content: A quintet of keyboards, saxophone, bass, drums, and percussion. A quartet with no percussion player from 1978. More drummers and a second bass on groove tracks.

content: Each member plays more than one instrument.
parameters: Shorter: soprano and tenor sax; Lyricon wind synthesizer on one track of 1976 (2 oscillators, filter, LFO, no envelope). Zawinul: Rhodes, piano, 2 ARP 2600, Oberheim, melodica, guitar, tabla, kalimba, tamboura, steel drums. Pastorius: fretless bass, mandocello, steel drums, drums. Andrew White: electric bass and English horn

where: The Inner Mounting Flame; Birds of Fire; Apocalypse

content: From a Latin group with voice and flute to an electric quartet. One player has nine keyboards.

content: Harp or organ with a drone instrument, bass, drums, and one wind soloist. Later a violin quartet.
parameters: 1970: harp or piano, soprano sax, double bass, drums, tanpura, bells and tambourine; oud on one track. 1971: harp and Wurlitzer organ (first use), 4 violins on 3 tracks (parts written out by Ornette Coleman), bass, 1 or 2 drummers, tanpura on 2 tracks

content: Electric bass, harp, strings and tenor saxophone play over laptop beats.
parameters: Thundercat bass on 8 of 17 tracks; Rebekah Raff harp on 8; Miguel Atwood-Ferguson strings on 5; Ravi Coltrane tenor saxophone on 2; guest keyboards on 2; trumpet, live drums and guitar on 1 track each

content: A jazz band plays with the keyboards, samples and laptop of the producer.

content: A laptop with Ableton Live is the centre. Analog keyboards and effects are around it. He plays drums by hand and does not quantise them.

content: Hollow-body six-string bass with magnetic and piezo pickups and a MIDI output. The high string gives room for chords.
parameters: Tuning B E A D G C (low to high); Ibanez custom model of 2012; hollow maple body; two EMG pickups plus a Graph Tech Ghost piezo and MIDI system; signature model Ibanez TCB1006; flatwound strings .029 to .128

content: Filter, octave and modulation effects make the bass sound like a synthesizer.

content: Six-string and fretless bass guitars, a hardware sequencer, and effect processors with his own algorithms.

content: He writes in trackers: lists of steps with commands, not a piano roll.
parameters: OctaMED on an Amiga 500; then MED Soundstudio on a PC; then Renoise; the 2016 album uses only a modular synthesizer

content: Sampler and sequencer with a grid of 16 pads. Each sound can have its own swing and its own shift.

content: Duo of bass guitar and drums with production and synthesizers. Guests add saxophone, guitar, trumpet and wind synthesizer.

where: Sungazer vol. 2 (2019); Perihelion (2021); Against the Fall of Night (2024)
